subject: Port MiSTer CPUFreq to Linux 6.18 with opt-in turbo (#85)
author: Kasper Olesen

upstream.vanilla_file_line: drivers/clk/socfpga/clk-periph.c:86-95 and drivers/cpufreq/Kconfig.arm, in vanilla 6.18.49 (release commit 1c732c6b94f0faee1526bd375add2fe10cba2e26, branch linux-6.18.y; verified with `git -C <linux> log -1` this session). No socfpga/altr/altera cpufreq driver exists in 6.18.49, and the gen5 socfpga clock driver has no .set_rate op.

provenance_doc_ref: docs/patch-provenance.md:789-875 (P1.6 cpufreq entry) and :798-804 (the 'P1.6 correction'); docs/abi-contract.md:1670

impact.effect_if_absent: None for our image: we already ship an equivalent capability (400/800/1000/1200 MHz, boost-gated) via 0003-cpufreq-cyclone5-de10nano-overclock.patch. What is absent without this commit is the fork's *implementation* - OCRAM-resident PLL retune under stop_machine with OUTRESETALL, 12.5%-per-step VCO ramping, bounded polling, rollback, and CCF rate-change notification to the A9 TWD local timers. Concretely, with 0003 instead of this: (a) the retune executes from DDR with the main PLL bypassed and jumps the VCO 25%/50% in one write; (b) the TWD clockevent rate is never updated, so at the 400 MHz operating point local-timer deadlines expire ~2x late and at 1200 MHz ~1.5x early; (c) the four wait_for_fsm() guards are no-ops (mask/bit-number bug, B6). For STOCK 6.18 users the commit restores a capability stock 20260907 shipped without at all.

userspace_coupling.interface: Standard cpufreq sysfs consumed by community overclock scripts on /media/fat: /sys/devices/system/cpu/cpufreq/boost, /sys/devices/system/cpu/cpu[01]/cpufreq/{scaling_max_freq,cpuinfo_max_freq,scaling_available_frequencies,scaling_boost_frequencies}. Main_MiSTer itself does NOT read cpufreq (no 'cpufreq' and no 'scaling_' anywhere in $S/main). Separate coupling for the DTS half of the commit: the fork claims the OCRAM tail holds MiSTer persistent flags; at Main_MiSTer 6cda9cc546c4b32e256a19931128b82586253812 the persistent-flags page is DDR physical 0x1FFFF000, not OCRAM.
userspace_coupling.main_mister_ref: fpga_io.cpp:397 (make_env: shmem_map(0x1FFFF000, 0x1000)); fpga_io.cpp:595-600 (reboot(): flg += 0xF08/4; *flg = cold ? 0 : 0xBEEFB001); user_io.cpp:1336 (sdram_sz, offset 0xF00); user_io.cpp:1370 (altcfg, offset 0xF04); fpga_base_addr_ac5.h:44 (#define SOCFPGA_OCRAM_ADDRESS 0xffff0000 - defined, never referenced anywhere in the tree)

forward_port.conflicts: None in the code half. `git show 59bcae8eb -- drivers/clk/socfpga drivers/cpufreq | patch -p1 -F0 --dry-run` against the 6.18.49 files applies all 10 files with zero fuzz, zero offsets, zero rejects. The two DTS hunks target the fork's own copy arch/arm/boot/dts/intel/socfpga/socfpga_cyclone5_de10_nano.dts (extra underscore) and do not apply to vanilla socfpga_cyclone5_de10nano.dts; the arch/arm/configs/MiSTer_defconfig hunk has no vanilla counterpart. Collision with our tree: drivers/cpufreq/Kconfig.arm and drivers/cpufreq/Makefile are already patched by our 0003 with a same-named CONFIG_ARM_SOCFPGA_CPUFREQ symbol at the same insertion point, and drivers/cpufreq/socfpga-cpufreq.c is created by both - 0003 must be retired, not co-applied.
forward_port.effort: M-L. Build verified this session: copied 6.18.49 source to a private tree, applied the code diff, copied board/mister/de10nano/linux.config + CONFIG_ARM_SOCFPGA_CPUFREQ=y, `make O=<tmp> ARCH=arm LLVM=1 olddefconfig` keeps it =y (SRAM=y already satisfied, linux.config:157), `prepare` rc=0, `make W=1 drivers/clk/socfpga/ drivers/cpufreq/` compiles clk-mister-cpu.o, clk-mister-ocram.o (AS) and socfpga-cpufreq.o with ZERO warnings. =y is viable: no request_module, no module-only assumption, and the late_initcall OCRAM setup lands after the built-in cpufreq device_initcall harmlessly (registration needs no OCRAM; the boot-time 400<->800 path is divider-only). clk-mister-cpu.c can only ever be built-in: it calls __arm_ioremap_exec(), which has no EXPORT_SYMBOL in 6.18.49 (arch/arm/mm/ioremap.c:421) - fine, since CLK_INTEL_SOCFPGA32 is bool (drivers/clk/socfpga/Kconfig:11-13). Remaining effort is the decision, the doc rewrite, and hardware validation at all four operating points.

notes:
DISPOSITION IS DELIBERATELY 'needs-verification': this is the owner's A/B/C decision (PLAN.md 2.4). The full comparison is docs/kernel-recon/fork-sync-2026-09/memo-Q4-cpufreq.md; do NOT close this record without reading it. Do not read 'needs-verification' as 'we might be missing a feature' - we are not; 0003 ships the same capability today.

THREE FINDINGS THAT REFUTE PARTS OF THE PLAN'S HYPOTHESIS.
(1) PLAN.md 2.4 and the option-C row assume the fork's driver changes the sysfs contract for community overclock scripts ('on upstream's driver scaling_max_freq alone may not reach 1200 MHz until boost is written'). FALSE - the two implementations are byte-identical on this axis. Both set .set_boost = cpufreq_boost_set_sw with .boost_enabled = false and flag the 1000/1200 rows CPUFREQ_BOOST_FREQ (ours: 0003-...patch:297-298 and :502-503; theirs: socfpga-cpufreq.c:12-13 and :51-52). In 6.18.49 the global /sys/devices/system/cpu/cpufreq/boost file is created purely from ->set_boost being non-NULL (cpufreq.c:2845-2847 cpufreq_boost_supported() returns cpufreq_driver->set_boost; :2943-2944 create_boost_sysfs_file()), a per-policy boost file too (:1107-1108 local_boost), and with boost off cpufreq_frequency_table_cpuinfo() skips the boost rows (freq_table.c:41-43) so cpuinfo.max_freq is 800000 and cpufreq_verify_within_cpu_limits() clamps any scaling_max_freq write to it (cpufreq.h:492/497-501 via cpufreq_frequency_table_verify(), freq_table.c:76). So on BOTH drivers `echo 1200000 > scaling_max_freq` alone yields 800000. Option C's stated rationale does not exist, and C would additionally re-create the auto-overclock bug our PR #24 fixed (cpufreq.c:1632-1634 -> policy_set_boost -> cpufreq_boost_set_sw at :2789-2797).
(2) docs/abi-contract.md:1670 is STALE and now says the opposite of what we ship: it claims 'there is no .../cpu/cpufreq/boost file' and 'OC is via scaling_max_freq up to cpuinfo_max_freq = 1200000'. That described 0003 BEFORE our PR #24 (3fb7f81/83ae09a). The shipped 0003 has .set_boost (0003-...patch:502), so the boost file exists and scaling_max_freq is capped at 800000 until boost is written. docs/patch-provenance.md:798-804 and :851-853 carry the same stale claim ('.boost_enabled = false is inert', 'does not exist (and never did)'). Fix regardless of A/B/C.
(3) The fork's stated rationale for the OCRAM tail reservation ('MiSTer uses flags at the end of OCRAM across core loads and reboots') does not verify against Main_MiSTer 6cda9cc54: the persistent flags live in DDR at 0x1FFFF000 (see userspace_coupling). The reservation is still worth carrying into 0004 as allocation hygiene - and it becomes load-bearing under option B, because their allocator rejects any OCRAM page outside 0xffff0000-0xffffefff (clk-mister-cpu.c:225-230) - but not for the reason given.

THE HANG QUESTION (PLAN.md 2.4, 'Whether our 0003 has that hang is an open question'). Their first attempt 'executed from DDR while gating FPGA-facing clocks, omitted OUTRESETALL and changed the VCO by 25% in one step'. Our 0003 does TWO of the three plus a fourth defect, and not the third:
  - DDR execution through the main-PLL bypass window: YES (0003-...patch:418-446 is plain kernel text; grep -c OCRAM -> 0; bypass asserted at :379-381 and :405-407).
  - Gating FPGA-facing clocks: NO. 0x60 (main-PLL group enable) and 0xa0 (periph group enable) appear nowhere (grep -c -> 0); the full offset list is :212-219. It rewrites the C5 divider at 0x5c (:392) UNGATED, which the TRM (quoted in the fork commit: 'C3-C5 require software gating') says not to do.
  - OUTRESETALL: NOT USED (grep -c OUTRESETALL -> 0). calculate_vco_reg() masks to 0x003ffff8 (:230, :311-313) so the reset bits are preserved untouched.
  - VCO in one step: YES, and worse. set_vco_freq() is a single writel (:410-411): 800->1000 is numer 63->79 = VCO 1600->2000 MHz (+25%, exactly their case); 800->1200 is 63->95 (+50%).
  - Fourth: wait_for_fsm() (:335-339) passes a MASK where wait_on_bit() wants a BIT NUMBER, so all four PLL settling waits are no-ops (B6, docs/patch-provenance.md:1522). Theirs uses bounded readl polling (clk-mister-cpu.c:89-90; clk-mister-ocram.S:134-146).
  - No stop_machine, no local_irq_save, no clk notifier in 0003 (grep -c -> 0 each): CPU1 keeps running DDR code with interrupts on through the transition, and because the CCF is bypassed the A9 TWD clockevent rate is never updated (socfpga.dtsi:861-866 twd clocks = <&mpu_periph_clk>, :286-291 mpu_periph_clk = mpuclk/4; smp_twd.c:110-138 only reacts to a clk POST_RATE_CHANGE notification). loops_per_jiffy IS corrected on both drivers via the ->target_index CPUFREQ_POSTCHANGE path (arch/arm/kernel/smp.c:794-841).

HARDWARE EVIDENCE WE ACTUALLY HAVE FOR 0003 ON 6.18: one data point, at 1200 MHz, and it was accidental. docs/testlogs/p1-first-boot.md:118 (DE10-Nano, real silicon, 2026-07-12, 6.18.33): 'the CPU is running at 1.2 GHz, so the PLL path evidently works'; same log :39 records cpuinfo_max_freq=1200000 with no boost file (the pre-PR#24 driver) and :41 a clean dmesg. That boot's 800->1200 transition is a +50% single-step VCO change from DDR without OUTRESETALL, and it completed. BUT the same auto-overclock behaviour also produced a field hard-hang, root-caused to running at 1.2 GHz on a passively cooled board (docs/debug-tooling.md:5-30, README.md:575) - nothing in our records isolates 'sustained 1.2 GHz' from 'the transition itself'. There is ZERO evidence at 1000 MHz, on either implementation, and no hardware test of 0003 at all after PR #24 made boost opt-in. Full doc sweep (grep -rn '1200|overclock|cpufreq' docs/*.md README.md docs/testlogs/*.md) yields only p1-first-boot.md:39/:118, debug-tooling.md:13, README.md:575, patch-provenance.md:1522.

THEIR UNRESOLVED ITEMS (from the commit message, all honest): long-duration 1200 MHz stability still under test; MiSTer Pi and SuperStation untested; 'OSD movement was reported during scripts' unexplained (no input injection; parallel evdev observer inconclusive under EVIOCGRAB); the corrected boost-off harness assertion (scaling_max_freq rather than cpuinfo_max_freq - i.e. exactly the ABI property above) has NOT been rerun. Code-level risks the memo adds: clk-mister-ocram.S:116-122 .Lhalt is a deliberate infinite loop inside stop_machine relying on a watchdog, and Main_MiSTer never opens one (grep -ri watchdog $S/main -> no matches) though we build CONFIG_DW_WATCHDOG=y (linux.config:375); mister_clock_fault (clk-mister-cpu.c:67, set at :263/:270) latches cpufreq dead until reboot; mister_flash_gates() returns -EBUSY if an enabled altr,socfpga-dw-mshc is sourced from the PLL being retuned (:146-149) - MiSTer always has an active SD controller, so whether CM_PER_SRC[1:0]==1 on a MiSTer board decides whether 1000/1200 work at all, and that is unverified; and the clk-side hijack is gated on IS_ENABLED(CONFIG_ARM_SOCFPGA_CPUFREQ), which is true for =m as well, so even an unloaded module changes the mpuclk ops and sets CLK_GET_RATE_NOCACHE on every gen5 pll/periph clock (clk-periph.c and clk-pll.c hunks).

SIDE-CHANGE (i), the DTS compatible: NOTHING TO CARRY. Vanilla 6.18.49 arch/arm/boot/dts/intel/socfpga/socfpga_cyclone5_de10nano.dts:15 already reads compatible = "terasic,de10-nano", "altr,socfpga-cyclone5", "altr,socfpga"; our 0004-dts-de10nano-MiSTer.patch:108 carries that line as unchanged context. Their hunk exists only because the fork keeps its own de10_nano.dts. Their code matches on that exact string (clk-mister-cpu.c:330 and socfpga-cpufreq.c:62 of_machine_is_compatible("terasic,de10-nano")), so our DTB already satisfies their matcher.

SIDE-CHANGE (ii), the OCRAM tail: CARRY INTO 0004 regardless of A/B/C, with the corrected rationale. We carry nothing equivalent today (grep -rln 'ocram|flags-sram' board/mister/de10nano/linux-patches/ -> no files; 0004 has no &ocram node). Vanilla socfpga.dtsi:785-788 is `ocram: sram@ffff0000 { compatible = "mmio-sram"; reg = <0xffff0000 0x10000>; }`. The mechanism checks out: drivers/misc/sram.c:199-225 records children with only 'reg' as reserved blocks and :291-321 skips them when populating the parent gen_pool (no export/pool/protect-exec => no subpool, no export, no clearing). Nothing else allocates from that pool on our image today (arch/arm/mach-socfpga/pm.c:50-57 is the only other consumer and we set '# CONFIG_SUSPEND is not set', linux.config:46). Exact node text is in the memo, section 6.

CONFIG POLICY: their =m defconfig commit (refs/pr/85 d49875d491) should be dropped if we adopt; =y is fully viable (see forward_port.effort). Their Kconfig adds `depends on CPU_FREQ && CLK_INTEL_SOCFPGA32 && SRAM` - SRAM=y is already set (linux.config:157).

WORKER RECOMMENDATION (advisory; the owner decides): A - keep 0003, record this as a deliberate divergence, and track B as a bench-gated follow-up. Strongest reason: the only user-visible thing B or C could buy (boost / scaling_max_freq semantics) is already identical between the two drivers, so B trades proven-in-the-field code (the only cpufreq code ever observed running a MiSTer at 1.2 GHz, including on our own board on 6.18) for better-engineered but entirely unvalidated code, on the one patch that can brick a board mid-transition. What would flip it to B: a reproducible hang/corruption on 0003 at 1000 or 1200 MHz on 6.18 hardware; evidence that the July field hard-hang was the transition rather than sustained 1.2 GHz; or a decision to converge our drivers/clk + drivers/cpufreq export with the fork's tree. Nothing flips it to C.

OWNER DECISION D1=A (2026-09-11), RECORD CLOSED. The owner read this record and memo-Q4-cpufreq.md and chose option A: keep 0003, do not adopt this commit's clk/cpufreq port. Disposition changed from needs-verification to dropped-deliberate accordingly (was NOT closed by this Wave-3 session's own analysis -- the analysis above is unchanged from the Wave-1/2 Opus pass; only the disposition and dependencies reflect the decision). Per the worker recommendation this record already carried: the driver comparison, the boost-ABI finding, and the DTS findings all stood without refutation through Wave 2.

WHAT 'DROPPED-DELIBERATE' MEANS HERE, PRECISELY. Only the DRIVER (the clk-mister-cpu.c/clk-mister-ocram.S/socfpga-cpufreq.c port, drivers/clk/socfpga/clk-periph.c+clk-pll.c hijack, and the defconfig's =m entry) is dropped in favour of the capability we already carry as 0003 -- see dependencies.superseded_by, which names 0003 and its own two origin records (3d72b9db7, e6df8e30e). The DTS half of this commit is NOT dropped: the &ocram flags-sram@f000 tail reservation (memo §6, corrected rationale -- Main_MiSTer's persistent flags are in DDR at 0x1FFFF000, not OCRAM, so this is allocation hygiene rather than a Main_MiSTer requirement under option A) IS carried, into 0004-dts-de10nano-MiSTer.patch, by the concurrent Wave-3 W3-0004 patch-authoring task. carried_patch stays null on THIS record because the schema's carried_patch/carried_mode pair describes one disposition for the whole commit and this commit's disposition is dropped (the driver); the DTS partial carry is recorded structurally in dependencies.superseded_by (the 'partial carry' entry naming 0004) rather than by setting carried_patch=0004, which would misstate that the whole commit -- driver included -- is carried. The `terasic,de10-nano` compatible hunk (side-change (i)) is NOT carried: vanilla 6.18.49 already has it (memo §6i; 0004 already carries the line as unchanged context).

OPTION B -- TRACKED, BENCH-GATED, NOT ABANDONED. Per memo-Q4-cpufreq.md §8's flip conditions, re-open this decision (re-evaluate B over A) the moment ANY of: (1) a reproducible hang or corruption on 0003 itself at 1000 or 1200 MHz on real 6.18 hardware (memo §8's hardware test script, 'boost on' section -- currently zero 1000 MHz data points exist on either implementation, the single largest evidence hole); (2) evidence the July field hard-hang (docs/debug-tooling.md:5-30, fixed by PR #24) was the PLL TRANSITION itself rather than sustained 1.2 GHz operation -- a serial capture at the moment of the frequency write would settle this; (3) a measured TWD timer defect under 0003 -- `( time sleep 1 )` reporting materially off 1.0s at the 400 MHz operating point (memo §1's stale-TWD-clockevent analysis, since 0003 never calls the CCF so smp_twd's clk-notifier-driven rate correction never fires); or (4) a decision to converge this repo's drivers/clk + drivers/cpufreq export with the fork's tree (e.g. to send patches upstream), which would make the divergence itself the cost regardless of hang evidence. None of the four are true as of this Wave-3 pass. Nothing flips this to option C -- memo §4 already refutes C's premise (the boost/scaling_max_freq sysfs contract is byte-identical between the two drivers; C would additionally re-create the PR #24 auto-overclock bug) and memo §8 says explicitly 'What would flip it to C: nothing.'
